question: A sold an article to B at 25% profit, who sold it to C at 20% profit. C sold to D at 45 % loss. If D bought it for ₹330 then B bought the article (in ₹) for:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Applying successive formula

A × (125)/(100) × (120)/(100) × (55)/(100) = 330

⇒ A = 400

⇒ CP for B = 400 × (125)/(100) = ₹500

∴ B bought the article for ₹500.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sold an article to B at 25% profit

B sold it to C at 20% profit

C sold is to D at 45 % loss

**Concept used:**

**1**. SP = CP × (100 + Profit)%

**2**. SP = CP × (100 - Loss)%

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the article to A be 100x

SP of A = 100x × (100 + 25)%

⇒ 100x × 125% = 125x

CP of B = 125x

⇒ SP of B = 125x × (100 + 20)% = 150x

CP of C = 150x

SP of C = 150x × (100 - 45)% = 82.5x

CP of D = 82.5x

⇒ 82.5x = 330

⇒ x = 330/82.5 = 4

CP of B = 125 × 4 = 500

**∴ B bought the article for ₹****500.**
